samples.summary: Report-before-push ordering makes the report's `Disputed (N)` count read 0 when the fixer files rebuttals after it
samples.evidence: `cmdPost` renders the body with `{ disputed: readRebuttals(pr).length }` (scripts/agent/fix-report.mjs:580 area) and `renderFixReportBody` prints `**Disputed (N)**` from that snapshot at post time (fix-report.mjs:426, rationale at :417-425 — the count exists precisely so "agreed with nothing" and "dispute channel is dead" stop looking alike). The new prompt hardens the report into a fixed slot ("AFTER COMMITTING, BEFORE PUSHING", panel yml:1665) while the rebuttal instructions still come *after* it in the prompt (agent-review-panel.yml:1696-1712) and the push section only requires that both are posted before the push (:1729-1734). A fixer that follows the prose literally posts the report first and any rebuttal second, so the maintainer-visible report always says `Disputed (0)` even when a dispute was filed seconds later. Fix belongs in the new prompt text: say rebuttals first, then the report, then the push.

samples.summary: The sibling on-demand fixer prompt still says "THEN REPORT" with the push described afterwards, so the two fixer prompts have diverged and only the panel one is pinned
samples.evidence: agent-fix.yml:333 ("THEN REPORT WHAT YOU DID") and :376 ("Pushing re-runs CI and a fresh review panel.") keep the old, unordered wording; checks.test.mjs:314-335 is the guard that exists to stop the two fixer prompts rotting apart, and it only checks that both contain `fix-report.mjs post`, so the divergence passes. The specific #757 race does not apply to agent-fix (its own group is `cancel-in-progress: false`, agent-fix.yml:78-80, and it is not in the panel's group), so this is consistency, not a live race — but the new test at fix-report.test.mjs:411 inspects only agent-review-panel.yml, so nothing keeps the two in step.
searchedFor: grep THEN REPORT WHAT YOU DID

samples.summary: The CI-arm fixer still has post-push work ("Then reply in the PR's verification thread") in a `cancel-in-progress: true` job, the same shape this change fixes for the panel fixer
samples.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:348-373 instructs push first and the PR-thread reply afterwards, and its `iterate` job is `concurrency: agent-iterate-<branch>` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:83-85). The window is much wider than the panel's because the workflow triggers on `workflow_run: [completed]` for CI (:19-22), so the cancelling run arrives minutes rather than ~30s after the push — which is why I rate this low confidence — but the post-push instruction is the same pattern the panel prompt just removed and was left unreviewed by this change.

samples.summary: A report now lands even when the push that should follow it fails, and `authorClaims` has no way to tell such a claim from a landed one
samples.evidence: `authorClaims`/`latestReport` (scripts/agent/fix-report.mjs:233-284) take the newest report at face value; the only staleness rule is "an older report is superseded" (fix-report.test.mjs:294-303 pins exactly that). With the report now posted before the push, a push that never lands leaves a `fixed` claim whose `head` still matches the branch, so it is not stale by that rule and would be handed to an adjudicator as a current claim about changes that are not in the tree (the panel's own no-commit page at agent-review-panel.yml:1806-1834 would fire on the same run). Adjudicators uphold by default and no new panel round runs without a push, so real impact is bounded — but nothing downstream distinguishes "reported and pushed" from "reported and failed to push".
